title: RCP org-scope Deny with INVERTED operator polarity (positive StringEquals footgun)
note: IAM-1302 iteration 2 (fixes review finding F1): a Principal-bearing, deny-only org RESOURCE guardrail whose org-scope condition uses a POSITIVE comparator (StringEquals aws:PrincipalOrgID) instead of the intended negated StringNotEqualsIfExists. In a Deny a positive comparator fires WHEN the org matches, so this policy denies requests FROM your OWN organization and PERMITS everyone else - the INVERSE of confused-deputy / org-perimeter protection, the exact StringEquals/StringNotEquals footgun. The evaluator must record operator polarity, narrate the inverted effect (NOT 'denies UNLESS the org matches'), stop asserting confused-deputy protection, and flag it as a misconfiguration hazard (severity medium, hazard=true), just as scp.js raises the over-broad-region hazard. The guardrail-not-grant invariant still holds: deny-only, empty graph, no S3/public-access finding, states a corresponding Allow must exist elsewhere.

rcpExpect.note: warned (not ok): the curated action catalog / condition classifier does not recognize the org-scope keys and the s3:* wildcard, an honest coverage gap - it does not weaken the guardrail semantics.
